thread:
Alex B: quick flag — telemetry shows a recent increase in sampled payloads that still contain unmasked PII for the /v1/chat route. noticed after the canary routing bump to dedicated nodes.
Mira P: ugh. are these coming from the fallback to dedicated or the new mux routing? any repro logs? :thinking_face:
Alex B: looks correlated with requests routed by policy:cost->dedicated when token_count > 2k. sampling rate went from ~0.5% to 3% for those routes.
Samir: important callout: our dedicated logging sink still gets full request/response for debugging by default. that sink doesn't run the same redaction pipeline as hosted. ops-bot: alert: ded-logs-sink ingestion rate increased 280% (last 1h).
Irene: so two risk factors: (1) route-level sampling increased fraction, (2) dedicated sink bypasses redaction. we should not log raw PII to the ded sink.
Mira P: quick proposal: add a per-route header we use in Router: `X-Redwood-Privacy: scrub=full|partial|none` and ensure ded-sink honors it. also add a console metric for sampled_vs_raw_ratio.
Samir: agree on header. also need a safe fallback if header missing. suggest default to `scrub=full` for any ded-routed traffic unless tenant has explicit inspect opt-in.
Alex B: +1. Can we patch the router policy config like this? snippet:
```
policies:
  - match: "/v1/chat*"
    route: dedicated
    privacy:
      scrub: full
      inspect_allowed: false
```

Irene: that snippet looks good. but we'll need a migration plan for existing dedicated clusters that currently expect raw logs for debugging. propose a 2-week roll where the ded-sink runs a pseudonymizer service in front of it (v1) and we flip a console toggle per-cluster.
Mira P: console UX idea: show a little badge on routes that indicates "Logs: masked / inspect-enabled / raw" and a button to request temporary inspect that creates a short-lived token audit. helps SREs request access without changing global flags.
Samir: ops question — how to handle historical sampled traces already in storage? do we redact retroactively or mark them for restricted access? both are painful.
Irene: mark restricted + backfill pseudonymization for highest-risk tenants only. full retro-redaction is a legal-heavy operation, need legal signoff.
Alex B: action items: (1) Samir, add `X-Redwood-Privacy` passthrough + default scrub policy in router (2) Mira, mockup console badge + temp-inspect flow (3) Irene, create ded-sink pseudonymizer design doc and opt-in migration plan. I'll kick off a quick canary to test header enforcement.
Mira P: thanks. tagging @security for visibility and @legal for the retro-redaction note. I'll add tiny mock in the console sandbox tomorrow.
ops-bot: scheduled job created: canary test route /v1/chat -> dedicated w/scrub header (start in 10m).
